api.flutter: SidebarProvider(children, defaultOpen=true, open, onOpenChange, variant=SidebarVariant.sidebar, minHeight) and Sidebar(children, side, variant, collapsible=SidebarCollapsible.offcanvas, expand=false) — enums SidebarSide{left,right}, SidebarVariant{sidebar,floating,inset}, SidebarCollapsible{offcanvas,icon,none}.
api.web: SidebarProvider writes document.cookie = `sidebar_state=${openState}; path=/; max-age=604800` on every setOpen call (line 105), persisting the panel's open/closed state across reloads for seven days; Sidebar takes the same side/variant/collapsible union-string props.

disabled.flutter: Sidebar/SidebarProvider/SidebarMenu carry no top-level enabled/disabled field; individual rows are Button instances which do have their own disabled path (audited under the button capability).
disabled.web: sidebar.tsx defines no disabled prop on Sidebar, SidebarProvider, or SidebarMenu; SidebarMenuButton forwards Button's own disabled handling rather than defining new disabled behavior.
disabled.note: The sidebar shell itself is not a control that can be disabled — disabled state belongs to the Button-based rows inside it, which are covered by the button capability's own audit file.

interaction.flutter: _SidebarProviderState installs a HardwareKeyboard.instance document-level handler for Cmd/Ctrl+B (SidebarProvider.shortcut = LogicalKeyboardKey.keyB) that toggles the sidebar from anywhere, matching window.addEventListener; _RailSlot's Semantics carries excludeSemantics: true, explicitly reproducing tabIndex={-1}.

semantics.flutter: SidebarTrigger builds an IconSwap(activeIndex: scope.open ? 0 : 1, icons: [panelLeftClose, panelLeft]) inside a Button(label: 'Toggle Sidebar') — a single static accessible name regardless of open/closed state — and _RailSlot's Semantics(button: true, label: 'Toggle Sidebar', excludeSemantics: true) matches the rail's static aria-label.
semantics.web: SidebarTrigger renders the IconSwap keyed on state plus a directional sr-only span reading 'Collapse sidebar' / 'Expand sidebar' rather than a static 'Toggle Sidebar', with the accompanying comment explaining aria-expanded was rejected because Button's ghost variant paints aria-expanded:bg-secondary permanently while the sidebar is open, so RULES §7's two-non-colour-signals rule is satisfied by the name instead.

ORIGINAL: The web's SidebarTrigger accessible name changes with state ('Collapse sidebar' / 'Expand sidebar'), which is the second, non-colour state signal RULES §7 requires; SidebarTrigger.dart always announces the static 'Toggle Sidebar' regardless of scope.open, so a screen-reader user gets no verbal confirmation of which way the control will move on the Flutter side even though the visual IconSwap glyph itself is faithfully ported. SidebarChrome.iconModeOf and SidebarScope.open are both already available in scope to fix this, so it is a straightforward, recorded gap rather than a platform limitation.
